faq.a: Sema is associated with the Arabic form سَمَا, whose core sense is sema; sky, heaven (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Sema?
faq.a: Sema is associated with Arabic. Sema is the Turkish form of Arabic سَمَاء (Samāʾ), meaning 'sky, heaven'; it occurs in the Quran.
Yes — the underlying form سَمَا is Arabic.
Sema can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sema should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Samāʾ occurs in the Quran as a term for the sky.
